verdict.label: not_replicated
verdict.rationale: Both randomized placebo-controlled trials examined dapagliflozin 10 mg versus placebo over 12 weeks and reported systolic blood pressure as an outcome, giving a comparable exposure, outcome, and between-group contrast despite different populations (kidney transplant recipients vs type 2 diabetes). Study A explicitly concludes no effect on the outcome: 'dapagliflozin did not lower systolic BP at 1 or 12 weeks' (an explicit substantive no-difference conclusion, distinct from its finding of reduced mean arterial pressure at 1 week). Study B reports a directional effect: dapagliflozin versus placebo showed 'improvements in ... systolic blood pressure (- 3.7 mmHg)' at 12 weeks, with no significance wording reported. An explicit no-effect conclusion in A against a reported effect in B places this pair in the not_replicated branch; no text-supported explanatory difference is specifically invoked by either abstract for the systolic BP result.

source_evidence.quote: Compared with placebo, dapagliflozin did not lower systolic BP at 1 or 12 weeks, although it did reduce mean arterial pressure after 1 week (3.9 mm Hg; 95% confidence interval [CI], -7.5 to -0.2).

After 12 weeks, patients randomized to dapagliflozin, as compared to those randomized to placebo, showed improvements in HbA1c (- 1.2%; 13 mmol/mol), systolic blood pressure (- 3.7 mmHg), and body weight (- 3.3 kg).

diagnostics.notes: Extraction checks passed on both sides: A's claim correctly captures the explicit no-difference assertion for systolic BP (sentence 9), and B's claim correctly captures the between-group -3.7 mmHg change with '-' orientation (sentence 11). The MAP reduction in A at 1 week is a separate finding and does not alter the systolic BP conclusion. Population difference (KTR vs T2D) is contextual and does not block comparison; no explanatory factor is specifically supported for the systolic BP discrepancy.
